name: – Eleonora Meleti, Rosa Estaràs Ferragut – After § 14 – Am 2
title: REPORT on advancing towards a care society: addressing the gender care gap
part_text: 14b. Stresses that the organisation of and access to care services fall within the competence of the Member States; considers that, in a context of limited public resources and increasing pressure on social systems, Member States should be able to apply the principle of national priority in the allocation of such resources, without prejudice to the rights of citizens from EU Member States, through objective criteria based on genuine attachment to the country, such as effective residence and contribution to the system, with a view to ensuring, first and foremost, adequate support for their citizens and legal residents; further underlines the sovereign rights of the Member States to limit access to structural services for those who do not fulfil the criteria to demonstrate such a link, while fully preserving assistance in situations of vital emergency, and to take into account the impact of migration flows from non-EU countries on the sustainability of public systems; emphasises, moreover, that the application of these principles and the organisation of labour linked to care services must not lead to social dumping, unfair wage competition or the undermining of workers’ rights and social standards within the EU, nor result in a disproportionate outflow of workforce between Member States, particularly in sectors already critically affected by labour shortages and demographic pressures, which could also lead to the mass impoverishment of families;
